articles.headline: Patriots CB Gonzalez says he's 'ready to go'; WR Brown returns to practice
articles.description: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez said Wednesday he's ready to return after missing the past two games with a shoulder injury.
articles.headlineJa: パトリオッツのCBゴンザレスが「準備完了」と表明、WRブラウンが練習に復帰
articles.descriptionJa: パトリオッツのコーナーバック、クリスチャン・ゴンザレスは水曜日、肩の負傷でここ2試合を欠場していたが、復帰の準備が整ったと語った。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez, who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury, said he will return for Sunday's home game against the New York Jets.

"I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday.

Gonzalez injured his shoulder in the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and initially thought he was OK after the game. He explained Wednesday what unfolded in the days following the game.

"At that point, you got a lot of adrenaline. Adrenaline covers a lot of things in this sport," he said. "At that time, I felt good. Things happen, so it is what it is and I'm ready for this week.

"... I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play. It's hard. You put in work with all these guys and then you don't get to be out there with them."

Gonzalez watched the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday from the sideline, saying it was important to him to be there for his teammates.

In addition to Gonzalez's return, receiver A.J. Brown is returning to practice for the first time since being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, according to coach Mike Vrabel. This is the first day Brown is eligible to return and Vrabel said he would "see how that goes" before determining if Brown plays Sunday.

Players were buoyed by news of Brown's return to practice.

"Huge boost. He's a receiver one," veteran safety Kevin Byard said. "Obviously the past couple weeks our pass game has been playing really well so he adds another dynamic to that."

In addition, second-year offensive lineman Marcus Bryant, who had been rolled up on in the preseason and was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return at the final roster cutdown, will also practice Wednesday. His return adds depth after starting left tackle Will Campbell was diagnosed with a sprained right MCL, a source told NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe. Campbell told reporters Wednesday that he was going to try to do some things at practice.

articles.headlineJa: スーパーボウルLXIのオッズ：全32チームの優勝確率
articles.descriptionJa: 全NFLチームの勝利予想数に加え、地区優勝、カンファレンス優勝、そしてスーパーボウルLXI制覇のオッズを掲載。
articles.body:
For the first time this season, the Los Angeles Rams are not the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI, as they have fallen to +700 after beginning the campaign at +500. The division-rival San Francisco 49ers are the new favorites at +680, having shortened after coming out of Week 5 tied with the Rams.

L.A.'s latest loss came via an overtime thriller Monday night to the Buffalo Bills, who are tied for the third-best odds on the board with the Baltimore Ravens at +800.

The next tier consists of the Kansas City Chiefs, who lengthened slightly from +900 to +950 during their bye week, and the Seattle Seahawks, who fell from +950 to 11-1 week-over-week after their close loss to San Francisco.

The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to gain ground after beginning the season at 30-1, making it all the way to 12-1. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings have also been a notable improver, tied with three other teams at 20-1 after coming into the campaign at 50-1.

The season's biggest disappointment is undoubtedly the Los Angeles Chargers, who began the season with sixth-best 17-1 odds and have fallen virtually out of contention to 200-1 after an 0-5 start.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

articles.headline: Barcola nets hat trick for 1st Liverpool goals in 6-goal UCL rout of LASK Linz
articles.description: Bradley Barcola got off the mark for Liverpool in spectacular fashion, scoring the first hat trick of his career in a thrilling 6-3 win at Austrian champions LASK Linz on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: バルコラがハットトリック達成、リヴァプールがUCLでLASKリンツに6ゴールで圧勝
articles.descriptionJa: ブラッドリー・バルコラがリヴァプールでの初得点を華々しく飾り、水曜日のオーストリア王者LASKリンツ戦でキャリア初のハットトリックを達成。チームは6-3で快勝した。
articles.body:
Bradley Barcola got off the mark for Liverpool in spectacular fashion, scoring the first hat trick of his career in a thrilling 6-3 win at Austrian champions LASK Linz on Wednesday.

Barcola, who arrived from European champions Paris Saint-Germain this summer in a deal worth a potential £123 million, had gone goalless in his first six appearances for Liverpool.

But he put that right to emphatic effect Wednesday, with his first hat trick in what was his 206th senior appearance.

The 24-year-old scored with either foot in the first half to open his account for the club against opponents making their debut among Europe's elite.

A far-post tap-in midway through the second half was the easiest of his three but by then his confidence was soaring, having missed a trio of chances in the win over Atlético Madrid last month.

While Barcola will grab the headlines, there was also a first Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo following his loan signing from Barcelona, while 21-year-old forward Lewis Koumas scored for the first time in the Champions League.

Liverpool's other goal came from Jeremie Frimpong, with Liverpool at one point holding a 6-1 lead.

LASK made the scoreline more respectable late on, thanks to a double from Florian Flecker.

The nine goals made it the highest-scoring European game for Liverpool since their 5-4 2001 UEFA Cup final win over Alavés.

Andoni Iraola's side, who bounced back from a 3-0 Premier League loss to Manchester City on Sunday, have begun the Champions League with back-to-back wins, following their opening victory over Atlético.

Iraola dropped Virgil van Dijk to the substitutes' bench on Wednesday with French defender Jérémy Jacquet starting. The Dutch star replaced Jacquet for the last half hour or so.

It was another central defender, Araújo, who broke the deadlock with a header from a corner, less than two minutes before Barcola got his first goal in the 24th from a lay-off by Koumas.

Ryan Gravenberch struck the post before Barcola got his second in the 37th, finishing with aplomb after being played through by Florian Wirtz.

Frimpong, one of the smallest players on the field, headed Liverpool's fourth in off the right post in the 51st.

Robert Ljubičić pulled a goal back in the 63rd, a minute after going on as a substitute, before Frimpong gave Barcola a simple tap-in to complete his hat trick in the 66th.

Koumas was left free to get Liverpool's sixth six minutes later, but Flecker -- another substitute -- got the biggest cheer when he scored his team's second with a diving header in the 74th.

ESPN Research, The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Real Madrid's Vinícius Junior gets 4-game ban after red card; will miss Clásico
articles.description: Vinícius Junior has been handed a four-game ban for his sending-off in Real Madrid's LaLiga win over Villarreal and will miss this month's Clásico with Barcelona.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールにレッドカードで4試合出場停止、エル・クラシコを欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールは、ラ・リーガのビジャレアル戦で退場となったため4試合の出場停止処分となり、今月行われるバルセロナとのエル・クラシコを欠場することになった。
articles.body:
Vinícius Junior has been handed a four-game ban for his sending-off in Real Madrid's LaLiga win over Villarreal and will miss this month's Clásico with Barcelona.

The Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee confirmed on Wednesday that the Madrid forward had been given a two-game ban for violent conduct after pulling Nathan Saliba's hair during Saturday's match at the Bernabéu, and another two games for his angry reaction to the decision.

Moments after the hair pull, Vinícius converted Jude Bellingham's pass to put Madrid 2-0 up, before a VAR review of the incident saw the goal disallowed, and the Brazil international shown a red card.

Coach José Mourinho had left Vinícius out of Madrid's starting XI for the game, after a difficult start to the season which has seen him score just once for his club.

Vinícius -- who apologized to fans on social media afterward -- will now miss Madrid's game with Sevilla on Sunday, and then the Clásico at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25, as well as matches with Racing Santander and Valencia.

The ban is only applicable in domestic competitions, so Mourinho named Vinícius in the starting XI for Wednesday's Champions League game at Roma. He will also be available for games with RB Leipzig on Oct. 21 and AEK on Nov. 4.

He will next play a LaLiga match after November's international break.

The committee said Vinícius had received a two-game ban for "violent conduct, without the possibility of playing the ball" and the two additional games for arguing with the referee "with an aggressive attitude and having to be restrained by his teammates."

Vinícius signed a new long-term contract at Madrid until 2032 this summer, after being heavily linked with a move away having entered the last year of his previous deal.

articles.headline: Sources: Man United assessing Lisandro Martínez comments
articles.description: Manchester United bosses are assessing Lisandro Martínez's comments in the aftermath of the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、リサンドロ・マルティネスの発言を精査
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの幹部らは、アトレティコ・マドリードに0-2で敗れた後のリサンドロ・マルティネスの発言を精査しており、このアルゼンチン人ディフェンダーに対し懲戒処分を下すかどうかを検討していると、情報筋がESPNに伝えた。
articles.body:
Manchester United bosses are assessing Lisandro Martínez's comments in the aftermath of the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender, sources have told ESPN.

Martínez criticised United director of football Jason Wilcox during a bombshell post-match interview on Tuesday night.

- Ogden: Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

The 28-year-old said he "expected more" from Wilcox during the summer transfer window and that the squad is not strong enough "to be ready for this kind of night."

Sources have told ESPN club bosses discussed Martínez's comments on Wednesday, which was a designated day off for the players.

The squad is due to return to the club's Carrington training base on Thursday with Martínez set to find out whether the club will take any further action.

Wilcox, meanwhile, retains the support of United chiefs, sources have told ESPN.

He arrived at Old Trafford as technical director in April 2024 before making the step up to director of football in December in the aftermath of Dan Ashworth's departure.

Ruben Amorim was sacked as head coach in January after his relationship with Wilcox broke down. It's understood that minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who was key to Wilcox's appointment, is happy with his role within United's hierarchy.

Brian is joined by ESPN's Vincent Goodwill and Tim MacMahon to preview the NBA's Central Division, including the biggest questions facing the five teams. Is this another make-or-break season for the Cleveland Cavaliers? Will the Detroit Pistons repeat their 2025-26 success? And, can Tyrese Haliburton's return vault the Indiana Pacers back up the Eastern Conference standings? They tackle all this and more in the latest episode of the Hoop Collective podcast.

Topics:

Windhorst on if the Cavaliers can improve their roster: "Jarrett Allen is the guy that they would have to do something with. And the thing about it is that they can't trade Jarrett Allen because you'd need a franchise center. And that means Evan Mobley would probably have to be your franchise center.

"First off, if you're trading Jarrett Allen, are you upgrading at center for trading Jarrett Allen? No, you're probably upgrading somewhere else and you're asking Evan Mobley to play center. And Evan Mobley has not proven, even though a lot of people believe that he would be at his best playing full-time stretch center, [he can do that]. That's not something they've been able to get Evan to do consistently well. But that's the move that they have. The move that they have if they have to do something is to look at Jarrett Allen.

"But we'll see how that plays out. The Cavs are in a tough spot in that they are going to be expected to improve on last season, which the pathway to improve on a conference final season, it's a narrow path. And they're doing it in a much more competitive Eastern Conference landscape."

articles.headline: Lamine Yamal: Assist for Anthony Gordon in Barcelona win 'almost-rabona'
articles.description: Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal christened his dribble leading to Anthony Gordon's goal against Galatasaray an "almost-rabona" as Barcelona ran out 4-1 winners in the Champions League game.

Yamal, 19, didn't score in the victory in Istanbul but produced a stunning second half display, setting up Fermín López with a pinpoint cross before creating for Gordon.

The teenager shaped to do a rabona, tricking the defender, only to knock the ball towards the byline instead. He benefitted from a small ricochet, but reacted quickly to drive inside before assisting the England international.

"I don't know what to call it, it was an almost-rabona dribble," Yamal told Movistar after the game as he watched a replay of the goal.

"It came off well to set up Gordon, that's the main thing, that it was effective at the end of the day."

In a separate interview with CBS, Yamal told former Barça forward Thierry Henry he is always looking for new ways to create space.

"Recently, I have noticed that a lot of opponents, whenever I reach the byline, go to ground, so I saw the opportunity, went for it and it came off," he added. 

"I always try to faint to create space. If you can create a bit of space that way, it gives us [attackers] life. It was nice, but also effective, so I am very happy."

- Flick urges caution as Barcelona extend perfect start with Champions League win

- Champions League recap: Atleti beat Man United, Viking snatch point vs. Bayern

- Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona chase Spurs defender Porro

In 10 appearances for Barça this season, Yamal has now scored eight goals and laid on nine assists.

Barça coach Hansi Flick credited him with "changing the game" against Galatasaray as the Spanish champions recovered from going behind to run out convincing winners.

"In the second half he was fantastic, how he dominated the game, the last pass ... It's unbelievable what he's doing," Flick said in the post game news conference.

The victory in Türkiye was Barça's 10th in a row at the start of the current campaign -- eight in LaLiga and two in the Champions League.

During that time, they have netted a remarkable 43 goals, with Yamal saying they are laying the foundations for potentially historic season.

"Always," he told CBS when asked if Barça believe a Treble -- winning LaLiga, the Champions League and the Copa del Rey -- is possible this season.

"We're Barcelona, we're the best team in the world."

That claim will be tested over the next week as Barça travel to third-placed Real Betis in LaLiga on Saturday, face Paris Saint-Germain in France in the Champions League next Tuesday and then host Real Madrid in the first Clásico of the season the following Sunday.

articles.headline: José Mourinho backs Vinícius Júnior to rediscover top form at Real Madrid
articles.description: Real Madrid coach José Mourinho believes it's only a question of time before Vinícius Júnior returns to top form.
articles.body:
Real Madrid coach José Mourinho said it's only a question of time before Vinícius Júnior returns to top form.

The Brazil forward, in his ninth campaign at Madrid, has set up three goals but scored just once in nine appearances this season.

"He is going to emerge," Mourinho said of Vinícius on Tuesday to TNT Sports. "It's just a question of when."

Mourinho was left encouraged by Vinícius' improved performance in Madrid's 1-0 home win over Villarreal on Saturday.

The Brazilian came off the bench and found the back of the net, only for the referee to rule it out because Vinícius had pulled the hair of a Villarreal player. As a result, the Brazilian was shown a red card.

"After the previous match [a 2-1 derby defeat at Atlético [Madrid] in which Vinícius started], I decided to take a different approach -- to protect him a little and then bring him on when the game called for a player like Vini," Mourinho said.

"I think that worked out well: the [Bernabeú] stadium, which had sometimes voiced disapproval, immediately rallied behind him the moment he started warming up. I believe that was a crucial turning point for him. He came on and played very well -- the goal and the sending-off were a shame, of course -- but it seemed like something clicked for him, reigniting that joy and reminding him of the kind of player he truly is."

- Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

- Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern

Mourinho, meanwhile, has issued a hands-off warning to any club wanting to sign Madrid forward Endrick in the next transfer window.

Endrick, 20, remained at the Bernabéu this summer despite being in high demand following a successful loan spell at Lyon in the second half of last season.

"Forget it, forget it -- forget about the clubs that are interested," Mourinho told TNT Sports when asked about the Brazilian's future.

"They'd better sit down and wait, or else they'll get tired. He's a player I adore, with incredible potential. And he's very important to us. Now, anyone interested in him will have to put up a real fight against me, because I believe he doesn't need to be loaned out and will be hugely successful here."

Endrick, who played at the 2026 World Cup with Brazil, has played only four minutes for Los Blancos this season.

He missed Madrid's opening four league games because of a muscular injury.

Asked about Endrick's limited playing time, Mourinho said: "After the preseason, he suffered an injury that sidelined him for over a month at the start of the season. And then -- it's true, I've spoken to him about this myself -- even after recovering, the right opportunity just hasn't come up ... In this [Villarreal] match -- luckily for us, but unluckily for him -- he was about to come on just as we scored.

"It happened practically the moment we got the goal. And then, when you're winning and down to ten men, it's natural for the coach to change his minds

articles.headline: Wemby, Spurs have 'clarity' after Finals loss but know 'nothing is guaranteed'
articles.description: The Spurs enter the season with expectations to return to the Finals after their loss to the Knicks.
articles.body:
IT'S A MUGGY Sunday in September at Frost Bank Center, and San Antonio Spurs media day is still a little more than two weeks away.

As the sun peeks through the arena's east entrance, condensation trickles down the floor-to-ceiling windows, a testament to the 86% humidity outside and similar to the pressure cooker inside the building for fans vying for a spot on Victor Wembanyama's official handpicked Spurs supporters group: the Jackals.

"This is something that hasn't been done to this level," said Aidan Sterling, president of the Jackals. "All the people who weren't Jackals last year, all the new guys, I know there's nerves amongst them."

Jitters would set in for some of the returning Jackals, too. Because unless they earned designation as "pack leader," membership isn't guaranteed this season, just like the Spurs aren't assured a spot in the 2026-27 NBA Finals after last season's shocking run that ended a six-year postseason drought and captivated fans.

"There's a lot of competition," said one of the Jackals' pack leaders. "Being a part of it last season doesn't guarantee you a spot this year."

It's a reality the Spurs understand all too well when measuring prospects for the upcoming season against the gauntlet that is the NBA's Western Conference, not to mention a vastly improved East or the fact that no team has advanced to the Finals in consecutive seasons since the 2018-19 Golden State Warriors. It's why Wembanyama and the rest of the squad tread carefully when discussing the sky-high expectations thrust upon the club in the wake of a 28-win improvement and Finals appearance. Wembanyama turned heads going into last season when revealing the team's goal of advancing to the postseason as a top-six seed.

Then, at September's media day, Wembanyama mentioned, "I couldn't imagine better motivation" coming off a 4-1 series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. The 22-year-old was the only Spur that day to openly discuss specifics regarding expectations for the upcoming season.

"We have some goals between us that we're going to keep between us as teammates," Wembanyama said. "We won the West last year. We don't want to do anything less this year. We want to be the first seed, and then we want to keep fighting for this top spot."

To do that, San Antonio plans to lean on process to spin success the way it has done for decades. It's the approach the Spurs used last season, focusing on internal improvement and the day-to-day to help them manage an 82-game regular season and an extended postseason.

In their minds, that's the only way to return to the game's grandest stage.

It's a methodology dating to former coach Gregg Popovich's 29-season tenure in which San Antonio established a South Texas dynasty that churned out five titles and a record-tying run of 22 consecutive playoff appearances.

articles.headline: Mikel Merino says Arsenal are 'ready' for Premier League, Champions League double
articles.description: Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.
articles.body:
Mikel Merino insists Arsenal are ready to go one better than last season and complete a Premier League and Champions League double.

Off the back of taking their first league title in 22 years, the Gunners have started this season with nine victories from 10 matches.

Arsenal's sole blemish so far arrived in a shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton which leaves them three points behind Manchester City in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta's men saw off Lille on Tuesday night to make it two wins from two in the Champions League.

The European triumph marked Arsenal's 14th consecutive victory in the group stage of the competition. The Gunners missed out on Champions League glory last term following an agonising penalty shootout defeat to Paris St Germain.

"It is an absolutely unbelievable run," said Merino of Arsenal's winning streak which stands at almost two years. "We know that we're making history.

"At the same time, we know how difficult it is to win games, so we give a lot of value and credit to the team for what we're doing.

"The goal and objective is to win the Champions League, to win the Premier League, to win everything. That's what the manager wants. That's what the fans want. That's what we as players want, too."

- Eberechi Eze on Arsenal competition: 'If you don't want to play you're not in the right place'

- Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern

And pressed as to whether he believes Arsenal are in a position to do that this season, the Spain international replied: "Absolutely. This is our mentality and the aim.

"We were so, so close last season. That proved to us that we are ready for it. Now it's about details. It's about being present and ready in the right moments, and of course we believe that."

Arsenal will bid to extend their winning run in the group phase to 15 when they travel to Germany to face Bayern Munich next week.

Before then, the Premier League champions will take on Nottingham Forest at the City Ground with midfielder Martín Zubimendi likely to be back in contention after he suffered an ankle injury in a training session following Arsenal's win against Leeds last weekend.

Piero Hincapié also suffered an ankle issue during the post-win training session at the Emirates Stadium.

"Zubi is much, much better," said Arteta. "Piero is improving, but it looks more significant. I think it will be a matter of weeks [before he is available], but we don't know exactly how many."

articles.headline: New era begins as Jayson Tatum and the Celtics embark on 1st season without Jaylen Brown
articles.description:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.


              COACH: Joe Mazzulla (5th season, 238-90).


              SEASON OPENER: Oct. 20 at Detroit.


              DEPARTURES: F Jaylen Brown, C Nikola Vucevic, F Anfernee Simons.


              ADDITIONS: F Paul George, C Mitchell Robinson, G Mike Conley Jr. 


              What to expect 
              It's a new era in Boston following the offseason trade of Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers. Only a few pieces remain from the core of the Celtics 2023-24 championship team. And there are lots of questions surrounding how this new version of the team will look without the homegrown tandem of Brown and Tatum that literally grew into the pillars of the franchise. Mazzulla has proven an ability to get the best out of what he has to work with, as evidenced in how the team played without Tatum last season as he recovered from rupturing his right Achilles tendon 17 months ago. But this may be the biggest test of Mazzulla's tenure as he looks to not only integrate new pieces, but make adjustments to an offense that has previously relied so heavily on 3-point shooting.


              Strengths and weaknesses


              The good: It starts with Tatum, who looks to be fully back to himself physically after rehabiliation from his surgery caused him to miss all but 16 regular season games and then Game 7 of their playoff loss to the 76ers because of a knee stiffness. George also enters the season healthy and at age 36 is poised to build off his strong playoff performance with the 76ers last season. Robinson’s presence brings an instant upgrade in rim protection, while also giving this group some great depth and options at center. Neemias Queta will likely remain the starter, but with plenty of support from both Robinson and Luka Garza. 


              The not-so-good: Brown’s departure breaks up the dynamic between he and Tatum that worked so well for nine seasons and eventually netted Boston its 18th NBA title. George says he’s more than willing to yield to Tatum, but that will put the weight on Tatum’s shoulders to carry the team, a burden he hasn’t had to bear alone yet during his career. 


              Players to watch
              Derrick White has tweaked the mechanics of his shot after a rough shooting year and will get more opportunities with Brown gone. Payton Pritchard started a career-high 50 games and average career bests in points (17.0), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season coming off winning NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024-25. Last season also showed that he plays better coming off the bench, a role he’s expected to remain in barring injuries. Hugo Gonzalez also looks more skilled and comfortable at the NBA level as he prepares for Year 2.
